findings.rationale: Compose-level Init aliases panic via .expect() instead of returning the documented CoreError. rewrite_compose_statements (line 952-961) maps resolve_alias_statement over the statements and calls .expect("compose alias validation occurs during lowering") on the collected Result at line 960. It is invoked from the ComposeItem::Common(SpecItem::Init) arm at line 345 with no surrounding error propagation, so a Result::Err there panics instead of returning. The documented contract (line 253-254 and the overview documented_contract) states lower_compose returns CoreError for 'unknown aliases'. The same unknown-alias condition is handled divergently for sibling items: ComposeItem::Common(Invariant/Trans/Reachable) routes through rewrite_compose_item (line 904-950) whose resolve_alias_expr(...) calls propagate with `?` (line 352, and 917/930/943), returning CoreError. Consequence: a SurfaceCompose whose top-level Init statement references a component alias not declared by any Use item panics, while the identical reference inside a top-level Invariant returns CoreError. The inline comment's claim that 'compose alias validation occurs during lowering' is not backed by any pre-validation pass present in the supplied windows, so the panic path is unguarded here. Concrete trigger: a top-level `init` containing an assignment or expression that names an undeclared alias.
